  artifact_coherence_checked_and_regenerated_on_the_cached_path = function() {
    bundle <- fixture_bundle()
    root <- tempfile("artifacts-")
    dir.create(root)
    cfg <- CONFIG
    cfg$output <- list(
      regs = file.path(root, "regs"),
      tables = file.path(root, "tables"),
      figures = file.path(root, "figures"),
      log = file.path(root, "log")
    )
    written <- export_artifacts(bundle, cfg)
    stamp <- as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
    Sys.setFileTime(written, stamp)
    status <- artifact_fingerprint_status(bundle, cfg)
    assert_true(
      status$current && length(status$reasons) == 0L,
      "a freshly exported set is current"
    )
    untouched <- ensure_artifacts_current(bundle, cfg)
    assert_true(
      !untouched$regenerated && is.na(untouched$reason),
      "a coherent set is not regenerated"
    )
    assert_true(
      all(abs(as.numeric(file.info(written)$mtime) - as.numeric(stamp)) < 1),
      "a coherent set is left untouched (mtimes unchanged)"
    )
    cells_csv <- file.path(cfg$output$tables, "cells.csv")
    df <- utils::read.csv(cells_csv, colClasses = "character")
    df$fingerprint[[1L]] <- "0000"
    utils::write.csv(df, cells_csv, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
    status <- artifact_fingerprint_status(bundle, cfg)
    assert_true(
      !status$current &&
        identical(status$reasons, "cells.csv carries a different fingerprint"),
      "a tampered CSV fingerprint is detected and named"
    )
    regenerated <- ensure_artifacts_current(bundle, cfg)
    assert_true(
      regenerated$regenerated && grepl("cells.csv", regenerated$reason),
      "the set is re-exported and the reason recorded"
    )
    assert_true(
      all(
        utils::read.csv(cells_csv, colClasses = "character")$fingerprint ==
          bundle$metadata$fingerprint$combined
      ) &&
        artifact_fingerprint_status(bundle, cfg)$current,
      "the re-exported set carries the bundle fingerprint"
    )
    unlink(file.path(cfg$output$figures, RUN_FINGERPRINT_FILE))
    unlink(file.path(cfg$output$log, RUN_LOG_FILE))
    status <- artifact_fingerprint_status(bundle, cfg)
    assert_true(
      !status$current &&
        length(status$reasons) == 2L &&
        any(grepl(RUN_FINGERPRINT_FILE, status$reasons)) &&
        any(grepl(RUN_LOG_FILE, status$reasons)),
      "a missing fingerprint file and log are named"
    )
    other <- bundle
    other$metadata$fingerprint$combined <- "ffff"
    assert_true(
      !artifact_fingerprint_status(other, cfg)$current,
      "artifacts of another run are not current"
    )
    assert_true(
      ensure_artifacts_current(bundle, cfg)$regenerated &&
        artifact_fingerprint_status(bundle, cfg)$current,
      "missing files are regenerated"
    )
    TRUE
  },
  unwritable_output_directory_fails_preflight = function() {
    root <- tempfile("output-")
    dir.create(root)
    writable <- file.path(root, "ok")
    assert_true(
      assert_output_dirs_writable(list(tables = writable)),
      "a writable directory (created on demand) passes"
    )
    assert_true(
      dir.exists(writable) &&
        length(list.files(writable, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE)) == 0L,
      "the probe file is removed"
    )
    readonly <- file.path(root, "ro")
    dir.create(readonly)
    Sys.chmod(readonly, "0555")
    on.exit(Sys.chmod(readonly, "0755"), add = TRUE)
    if (file.access(readonly, 2L) != 0L) {
      # not running as a user that ignores permissions
      assert_error_matching(
        assert_output_dirs_writable(list(ok = writable, ro = readonly)),
        "not writable: .*/ro",
        "a read-only directory is named"
      )
      assert_error_matching(
        assert_output_dirs_writable(list(file.path(readonly, "child"))),
        "not writable",
        "a directory that cannot be created is named"
      )
    }
    TRUE
  },
  fixture_suite_names_unique_and_scenarios_return_true = function() {
    assert_true(
      length(FIXTURE_CHECKS) > 0L && all(lengths(FIXTURE_CHECKS) > 0L),
      "the suite and every unit are non-empty"
    )
    for (unit in names(FIXTURE_CHECKS)) {
      scenarios <- names(FIXTURE_CHECKS[[unit]])
      assert_true(
        !is.null(scenarios) &&
          all(nzchar(scenarios)) &&
          anyDuplicated(scenarios) == 0L,
        paste("scenario names are unique and non-empty in", unit)
      )
    }
    assert_error_matching(
      run_fixture_checks(list(x = list(silent = function() invisible(NULL)))),
      "x / silent: scenario did not return TRUE",
      "a scenario that does not return TRUE fails"
    )
    assert_error_matching(
      run_fixture_checks(list(
        x = list(dup = function() TRUE, dup = function() stop("never run"))
      )),
      "duplicated scenario name\\(s\\) in x: dup",
      "duplicated scenario names are refused"
    )
    assert_error_matching(
      run_fixture_checks(list()),
      "no fixture checks",
      "an empty suite is refused"
    )
    assert_error_matching(
      run_fixture_checks(list(x = list())),
      "no fixture checks",
      "an empty unit is refused"
    )
    ok <- run_fixture_checks(list(x = list(fine = function() TRUE)))
    assert_true(
      nrow(ok) == 1L && isTRUE(ok$passed),
      "a TRUE-returning scenario passes"
    )
    TRUE
  }
)

fixture_results <- run_fixture_checks(FIXTURE_CHECKS)

#| label: fixtures-only-exit

# `-P fixtures_only:true` renders the synthetic checks alone: no data is read and
# no bundle is loaded or written. Display/control only; not fingerprinted.
fixture_display <- dplyr::mutate(
  fixture_results[, c("unit", "scenario", "passed")],
  passed = ifelse(passed, "yes", "no")
)
unit_counts <- table(fixture_display$unit)
emit_paragraph(sprintf(
  paste(
    "**Fixtures-only render:** %d synthetic fixture checks passed (%s).",
    "No input was read and no bundle was loaded or written; the rest of",
    "the report is omitted."
  ),
  nrow(fixture_display),
  paste(
    sprintf("%s: %d", names(unit_counts), as.integer(unit_counts)),
    collapse = ", "
  )
))
emit_table(knitr::kable(
  fixture_display,
  format = "html",
  caption = "Fixture checks (synthetic data)"
))
knitr::knit_exit()

```{r}
#| label: estimate
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr params$reestimate

# Per-market loop (U1 readiness -> U2 exposure and attention; U3 adds fitting).
# Shared inputs are loaded once; each market's pre-band panel is released as
# soon as the bands are applied.
run_started <- Sys.time()
assert_output_dirs_writable(CONFIG$output) # fail before the long run, not after it
site_projection <- load_site_projection(
  CONFIG$crosswalk_path,
  CONFIG$crosswalk_years
)
article_input <- load_article_monthly(CONFIG$articles_path)
article_validation <- validate_article_input(article_input$monthly)
article_evidence <- article_export_evidence(
  CONFIG$article_zip_dir,
  CONFIG$article_records_path,
  CONFIG$articles_path
)
attention_calendars <- lapply(MARKETS, function(m) {
  build_attention_calendar(
    m,
    article_input$monthly,
    article_evidence,
    article_validation
  )
})
names(attention_calendars) <- MARKETS
input_provenance <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  site_projection$provenance,
  article_input$provenance,
  article_evidence$provenance
)

readiness <- list()
observation_diagnostics <- list()
exclusion_ledger <- new_ledger()
profile_exclusion_ledger <- new_ledger()
variant_ledger <- new_variant_ledger()
market_data <- list()
cells <- list()
profiles <- list()
residual_support <- list()
residual_support_by_year <- list()
samples <- list()
models <- list()
fit_logs <- list()
for (market in MARKETS) {
  started <- Sys.time()
  prepared <- prepare_market_panel(market)
  readiness[[market]] <- prepared$readiness
  observation_diagnostics[[market]] <- prepared$diagnostics
  input_provenance <- dplyr::bind_rows(input_provenance, prepared$provenance)
  entry <- list(
    market = market,
    status = prepared$status,
    reason = prepared$reason,
    panel = NULL,
    change_flags = NULL,
    ledger = prepared$ledger,
    readiness = prepared$readiness,
    diagnostics = prepared$diagnostics,
    exposure_summary = NULL,
    calendar = attention_calendars[[market]],
    profile_panel = NULL,
    profile_ledger = prepared$profile_ledger
  )
  if (prepared$status == "ready") {
    exposure <- apply_exposure(
      prepared$panel,
      site_projection$projection,
      prepared$ledger,
      market
    )
    profile_panel <- prepared$profile_panel
    profile_ledger <- prepared$profile_ledger
    rm(prepared)
    invisible(gc())
    panel <- attach_attention(exposure$panel, attention_calendars[[market]])
    entry$panel <- panel
    entry$change_flags <- exposure$change_flags
    entry$ledger <- exposure$ledger
    entry$distance_summary_all <- exposure$distance_summary_all
    entry$exposure_summary <- exposure_summaries(panel, market)
    rm(exposure, panel)
    # The separate annual-profile panel takes the same fixed exposure and the
    # same band and two-distinct-dates steps, but no attention join: its
    # earlier months lie outside the article calendar by design (AE3).
    if (!is.null(profile_panel)) {
      profile_exposure <- apply_exposure(
        profile_panel,
        site_projection$projection,
        profile_ledger,
        market
      )
      entry$profile_panel <- prune_profile_panel(profile_exposure$panel)
      entry$profile_ledger <- profile_exposure$ledger
      rm(profile_exposure)
    }
    rm(profile_panel, profile_ledger)
    invisible(gc())
  } else {
    rm(prepared)
  }
  # U3: the model grid on this market (blocked markets receive blocked_input cells).
  fitted <- estimate_market_models(entry, market)
  cells[[market]] <- fitted$cells
  profiles <- c(profiles, fitted$profiles)
  residual_support[[market]] <- fitted$residual_support
  residual_support_by_year[[market]] <- fitted$residual_support_by_year
  samples[[market]] <- fitted$samples
  models <- c(models, fitted$models)
  fit_logs[[market]] <- dplyr::mutate(
    fitted$fit_log,
    market = market,
    .before = 1L
  )
  variant_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(variant_ledger, fitted$ledger)
  rm(fitted)
  entry$panel <- NULL
  entry$profile_panel <- NULL
  entry$runtime_seconds <- as.numeric(difftime(
    Sys.time(),
    started,
    units = "secs"
  ))
  exclusion_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(exclusion_ledger, entry$ledger)
  profile_exclusion_ledger <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    profile_exclusion_ledger,
    entry$profile_ledger
  )
  market_data[[market]] <- entry
  rm(entry)
  invisible(gc())
}
assert_ledger_identity(exclusion_ledger)
assert_ledger_identity(profile_exclusion_ledger)
cells <- dplyr::bind_rows(cells)
residual_support <- dplyr::bind_rows(residual_support)
residual_support_by_year <- dplyr::bind_rows(residual_support_by_year)
fit_logs <- dplyr::bind_rows(fit_logs)
assert_model_grid_complete(cells, profiles)

# U4: bind the run's identity to every planned cell, save atomically, export artifacts.
peak_gc_mb <- max(
  c(
    fit_logs$peak_gc_mb,
    vapply(readiness, function(r) r$peak_memory_mb %||% NA_real_, numeric(1))
  ),

)
runtime <- list(
  started_at = format(run_started, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
  finished_at = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"),
  total_seconds = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), run_started, units = "secs")),
  peak_gc_mb = peak_gc_mb,
  peak_memory_note = sprintf(
    "peak R heap during the run (gc) was %s MB; the OS-level peak footprint is higher and is measured outside R, for example with /usr/bin/time -l",
    format_count(round(peak_gc_mb))
  )
)
bundle <- assemble_bundle(
  site_projection = site_projection,
  article_validation = article_validation,
  article_evidence = article_evidence,
  attention_calendars = attention_calendars,
  input_provenance = input_provenance,
  readiness = readiness,
  observation_diagnostics = observation_diagnostics,
  exclusion_ledger = exclusion_ledger,
  variant_ledger = variant_ledger,
  market_data = market_data,
  cells = cells,
  profiles = profiles,
  residual_support = residual_support,
  residual_support_by_year = residual_support_by_year,
  samples = samples,
  models = models,
  fit_log = fit_logs,
  fixture_checks = fixture_results[, c("unit", "scenario", "passed")],
  runtime = runtime,
  fingerprint = compute_fingerprint(input_provenance, rehash = FALSE),
  profile_ledger = profile_exclusion_ledger
)
bundle <- complete_bundle(bundle)
save_bundle_atomic(bundle, file.path(CONFIG$output$regs, CONFIG$bundle_file))
export_artifacts(bundle)
cat(sprintf(
  "Bundle saved (fingerprint %s, %.0f s); artifacts exported.\n",
  bundle$metadata$fingerprint$combined,
  runtime$total_seconds
))
# Release the in-memory results: every display chunk reads the bundle loaded from disk.
rm(

  site_projection,

  article_evidence,

  input_provenance,

)

cell_phrase <- function(key, digits = 4) {
  status <- cell_value(key, "status")
  if (!status %in% ESTIMATED_STATUSES) {
    return(sprintf("not estimated (%s)", status))

  est <- cell_value(key, "estimate")
  if (status == "estimated_inference_unavailable") {

The model grid has `r nrow(cells)` scalar cells (`r status_phrase`) and `r length(results$profiles)` annual profiles (`r profile_status_phrase`). The scalar cells use the 2014-onward samples; the sales profiles use the separate 1995–2024 profile panel and the rental profiles the 2014–2023 panel. Every planned cell is accounted for below; cells that could not be estimated keep their status and reason rather than a substituted number.

```{r}

#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: !expr coefficient_caption

plot_coefficients(cells)
```

```{r}
#| label: findings-headline-table
#| results: asis

knitr::kable(
  headline_table(cells),
  format = "html",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Headline cells: eligible long-run repeat properties, no controls. Ratio change (%) = 100 (exp(beta) - 1) for post cells, the change in the conditional near/far price ratio."
)
```

**Post indicator.** Under property and calendar-month effects the headline near–far gap changes by `r cell_phrase(key_s_pm_post)` log points for sales and `r cell_phrase(key_r_pm_post)` for rentals from August 2022; as changes in the conditional near/far price ratio these are `r ratio_phrase(key_s_pm_post)` and `r ratio_phrase(key_r_pm_post)`. Adding MSOA × year effects moves the sales coefficient to `r cell_phrase(key_s_my_post)` and the rental coefficient to `r cell_phrase(key_r_my_post)`, so the within-property post gap under the fuller structure is `r ratio_phrase(key_s_my_post)` for sales and `r ratio_phrase(key_r_my_post)` for rentals. The translation is a change in the near/far ratio, not an absolute fall in near-property prices.

**Article stock.** The article coefficient is the change in the gap per log point of the cumulative search-1 stock (`r format_count(stock_event)` articles by `r format(CONFIG$event_month, "%B %Y")`, `r format_count(sales_stock_end)` by the end of the sales calendar), not the effect of one additional article. The headline estimates are `r cell_phrase(key_s_pm_art)` (sales) and `r cell_phrase(key_r_pm_art)` (rentals) with property and month effects, and `r cell_phrase(key_s_my_art)` and `r cell_phrase(key_r_my_art)` with MSOA × year effects.

```{r}
#| label: findings-profile-plot
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr profile_caption

profile_plot <- plot_profiles(results$profiles)
if (is.null(profile_plot)) {
  cat(
    "No annual profile was estimable; the profile tables record the reasons.\n"
  )
} else {
  profile_plot
}
```

**Reading these results.** Two features of the grid matter more than any single coefficient. First, the sign and size of the post and article coefficients depend on the fixed-effect structure: the MSOA × year effects absorb local annual price paths, and what remains is the within-property, within-MSOA-year near–far change. Second, the annual profiles show how the near–far gap moved before 2022, for sales over the full 1995–2024 history; the joint test above covers only 2014–2018 relative to 2019 (computed on the expanded sales fit's covariance for sales), the 2022 coefficient mixes pre- and post-August months, and neither is a test of parallel trends over all pre-event observations. Sales coefficients from 2014 onward in the profiles are not the scalar-sample coefficients re-expressed: the expanded panel adds properties whose histories connect through earlier sales, so they may differ from a 2014-only profile. The sample variants (excluding observed characteristic changes, complete cases with and without controls, the 2021-on window) show how far each estimate depends on sample composition; differences in statistical significance between variants do not establish differences between estimates.

None of this is presented as evidence of a publicity effect. Property effects remove fixed proximity and fixed characteristics, calendar-month effects remove national shocks common to near and far properties, and MSOA × year effects remove local annual paths, but competing changes in the relative desirability of near locations over the same period are not excluded. These are unweighted transaction-level fixed-effects projections: the frequency and timing of repeat observations, not equal property weights, determine the implicit weighting.

## Design

For property $i$ observed in calendar month $m$ the scalar cells estimate

$$
\log p_{im} = \alpha_i + \lambda_m + \beta\,(\mathrm{Near}_i \times A_m) + \varepsilon_{im},
$$

and, under the second fixed-effect structure,

$$
\log p_{im} = \alpha_i + \lambda_m + \gamma_{g(i),\,y(m)} + \beta\,(\mathrm{Near}_i \times A_m) + \varepsilon_{im},
$$

where $\gamma_{g(i),y(m)}$ is an MSOA × calendar-year effect. The annual profiles replace the single interaction by year-specific ones, on the rental headline sample and on the separate 1995–2024 sales profile panel (the same sample and exposure rules applied to the longer sales history, repeats recomputed within it):

$$
\log p_{im} = \alpha_i + \lambda_m + \left[\gamma_{g(i),\,y(m)}\right] + \sum_{y \neq `r CONFIG$profile_reference_year`} \delta_y\,(\mathrm{Near}_i \times \mathbb{1}\{y(m) = y\}) + \varepsilon_{im}.
$$

- $p_{im}$: sale price (sales) or listing price at `rented_est` (rentals), in logs; finite positive outcomes only.
- $\alpha_i$: property (repeat-group) effect; it absorbs the near main effect and every fixed characteristic.
- $\lambda_m$: calendar-month effect, indexed as consecutive calendar months with January 2014 = 1 (the sales profile panel uses indices from January 1995; no article record is needed for a month); it absorbs the attention main effect.
- $\mathrm{Near}_i$: 1 for the `r CONFIG$bands$near_min`–`r CONFIG$bands$near_max` m band, 0 for the `r format_count(CONFIG$bands$far_min)`–`r format_count(CONFIG$bands$far_max)` m band, from the fixed Site Group projection; the intervening band and everything beyond `r format_count(CONFIG$bands$far_max)` m are dropped.
- $A_m$: the post indicator (1 from `r format(CONFIG$event_month, "%B %Y")` inclusive) or $\log$ of the cumulative search-1 article count from `r format(CONFIG$article_origin, "%B %Y")`, evaluated through the full transaction or listing month.
- $\delta_y$: the near–far gap in year $y$ relative to `r CONFIG$profile_reference_year`.

| Variant | Sample | Controls | Purpose |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Headline | Eligible long-run repeat properties (two distinct dates in the banded panel) | None | Main within-property comparison |
| Exclude observed changes | Headline less whole properties with any observed characteristic change (sales: property type; rentals: type, bedrooms, bathrooms), repeats recomputed | None | Sensitivity to recorded changes |
| Complete-case comparator | Rows with nonmissing controls, repeats recomputed | None | Isolate complete-case selection |
| Complete cases with controls | Exactly the comparator's estimation rows within each fixed-effect structure | Sales: type, old/new, tenure; rentals: type, bedrooms, bathrooms | Isolate adding observed characteristics |
| Short window | `r format(CONFIG$short_window_start, "%B %Y")` through each market's end, repeats recomputed, same article stock | None | Compare the period used by the existing news analysis |

```{r}
#| label: design-inference
#| results: asis

reference_model <- Filter(
  function(m) !is.null(m) && !is.null(m$ssc),
  results$models
)
if (length(reference_model) > 0L) {
  ssc <- reference_model[[1L]]$ssc
  inference_rows <- tibble::tibble(
    item = c(
      "Covariance",
      "Small-sample correction (fixest ssc)",
      "Degrees of freedom for intervals and p-values",
      "95% interval",
      "Joint test"
    ),
    value = c(
      "Clustered by LSOA on each fit's actual estimation sample",
      paste(
        sprintf(
          "%s = %s",
          names(ssc),
          vapply(
            ssc,
            function(v) paste(format(v), collapse = "/"),
            character(1)
          )
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      "The model's clustered t degrees of freedom (recorded per cell as `t df`)",
      "estimate ± t(0.975, df) × clustered standard error, pointwise",
      sprintf(
        "Wald F on the %s Near x year coefficients with the full clustered covariance block; unavailable, not reduced, when a contrast or the block is unavailable",
        paste(range(CONFIG$profile_joint_years), collapse = "-")
      )
    )
  )
  emit_table(knitr::kable(
    inference_rows,
    format = "html",
    caption = "Inference conventions (KTD11)"
  ))
} else {
  cat("No fitted model carries inference settings in this bundle.\n\n")
}
```

**Residual support (KTD11).** For every scalar fit the focal regressor $\mathrm{Near}_i \times A_m$ is residualised on all included fixed effects and controls over the fit's actual sample. The report records the residual sum of squares, its ratio to the centred raw variation of the same regressor, and the shares of the squared residuals by calendar year and by LSOA cluster. These are descriptive measures of how much and where design variation remains; no threshold, weight or exclusion follows from them and they do not establish identification.

    nrow(cells)

### Sample support

The support table reports, for every cell, the rows the estimator used, the properties and LSOA clusters behind them, near and far property counts, properties observed on both sides of `r format(CONFIG$event_month, "%B %Y")`, rows removed by the estimator (fixed-effect singletons), and controls absorbed by the fixed effects. Absorption of a control does not invalidate the focal coefficient, and none of these counts establishes identification on its own.

```{r}
#| label: results-support-table
#| results: asis

support_table <- cell_order(label_cells(cells)) |>

### Annual profiles with alternative reference years

These two additional views describe the same annual near–far price paths using different comparison years. The 2014 reference is a comparison year: the first year of the scalar samples and the year after the 2013 sector-wide monitoring instruction, not the start of the sales profile sample (which begins in 1995) and not a pre-monitoring-policy baseline. The 2021 reference compares each year with the last full calendar year before the August 2022 attention spike. Neither reference assigns a causal effect to monitoring or publicity.

Each contrast is the difference between two coefficients from the original model. Its pointwise 95% interval uses the full LSOA-clustered covariance, including the covariance between those coefficients, and the original model's t degrees of freedom. The hollow point fixes the reference year at zero; it is a normalization, not an estimate with no uncertainty. Each market uses matching vertical scales across the two figures. The original 2019 profiles, joint tests, samples and main analyses are unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-profile-reference-views
#| include: false

reference_profile_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(2014L, 2021L), function(year) {
  profile_reference_rows(results$profiles, year)
}))
reference_profile_limits <- profile_reference_limits(reference_profile_rows)
reference_profile_plots <- lapply(c(2014L, 2021L), function(year) {
  plot_profile_reference(reference_profile_rows, year, reference_profile_limits)
})
names(reference_profile_plots) <- c("2014", "2021")
# Export these display-only additions on both fresh and validated cached renders.
for (year in c(2014L, 2021L)) {
  save_figure_pdf(
    plot_profile_reference(reference_profile_rows, year, reference_profile_limits, base_size = 8),
    file.path(CONFIG$output$figures, sprintf("annual_profiles_reference_%d.pdf", year)),
    width_cm = 14.5,
    height_cm = 9
  )
}
```

```{r}

The hollow point is the reference-year normalization; the vertical line marks August 2022, while the 2022 estimate covers the full calendar year."

## Sample flows and readiness

The inputs are the two long-run transaction histories and their repeat mappings. Every number in this section is computed from those files when the bundle is built; none is typed in. A market is marked *blocked* when a validation step fails, and its model cells are then reported as blocked rather than estimated on a substituted sample.

#### Current-address verification

Address keys and expected repeat ids are recomputed read-only on every requested-window row that is in the mapping, singles included, with the production `build_address_key()` and `hash_serialized_values()` contract and the market's exact field order. Any missing current key or mismatched repeat id blocks the market; nothing is rebuilt or repaired here.

```{r}

#| results: asis

    market = m,
    status = a$status,
    candidates = a$n_candidates,
    candidate_groups = a$n_candidate_groups,
    window_singles = a$n_window_singles,
    missing_current_keys = a$n_missing_keys,
    mismatched_repeat_ids = a$n_mismatched,
    mismatched_groups = a$n_mismatched_groups
  )
}))
emit_table(knitr::kable(
  address_rows,
  format = "html",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "KTD10 current-address verification on requested-window mapped candidates"
))

### Exposure

Exposure is fixed from overflow locations alone. The Site Group crosswalk for `r paste(range(CONFIG$crosswalk_years), collapse = "–")` is projected to one representative location per Site Group with the existing latest-valid rule; `annual_status` is read only so that the projection helper can validate the crosswalk's structure, and no monitoring, spill or availability information enters eligibility (AE3). Each unique property coordinate is matched to its nearest usable Site Group with an STRtree-indexed nearest-feature search in British National Grid metres. The two-distinct-dates requirement is recomputed on the banded panel, and characteristic-change flags are frozen on that eligible long-run panel before any complete-case or short-window restriction.

```{r}
#| label: exposure-projection
#| results: asis

sp <- results$site_projection
projection_rows <- tibble::tibble(
  item = c(
    "Crosswalk rows read",
    "Configured years",
    "Site Groups",
    "Usable locations (finite easting and northing)",
    "Site Groups without a valid location (counted, omitted from matching)",
    "Water companies",
    "Location rule",
    "Property coordinates",

### Attention calendar

The attention measures are a post indicator (`r format(CONFIG$event_month, "%B %Y")` onward, set from the configured event month and independent of any helper's base year) and the log of the cumulative count of search-1 LexisNexis articles from `r format(CONFIG$article_origin, "%B %Y")`. The stock excludes every earlier article. Absent months are filled with zero only inside established coverage of this fixed corpus, which is recomputed when the bundle is built from the export zips: `.docx` entries across the zips (one article each) that equal the extracted article rows, a date on every extracted article, an article-level monthly count that reproduces the monthly file, and an export date read from the zip entry timestamps. The DOCX exports carry no cover page, so the search terms and any date narrowing are not checked against the export. Observed first and last article dates never stand in for that evidence. When any check fails, the article cells are blocked and the post and annual-profile analyses continue.

Established coverage certifies only that the extraction matches the export of this one Boolean search at export time. The documented LexisNexis refinement work records off-topic matches and merged article boundaries with potentially misassigned metadata in this corpus; those limits are inherited here without filtering or repair, and the counts do not certify comprehensive or compositionally constant UK media coverage.

## Limitations

**Measurement.** Property coordinates are postcode centroids, so distances to the mapped representatives are approximate and dwellings around a band boundary can be misclassified; "far" means far from a usable mapped Site Group representative, not verified absence of a closer unmapped overflow, and the small count of Site Groups without a valid location does not bound that error. Repeat groups are operational address matches (postcode plus address fields), not verified immutable dwellings or independent rental episodes; the address-key verification is a construction check, not independent evidence of dwelling identity. The rental outcome is a listing price whose unit is not documented by the provider; the report checks continuity across the 2022/2023 vintage boundary and applies no conversion, and its date is `rented_est` (`rented` with a `latest_to_rent` fallback whose share is reported by year and band), which establishes neither the agreed rent nor an exact tenancy start. The article series is one fixed LexisNexis Boolean search whose coverage is established only through the export evidence above; off-topic matches and merged article boundaries in that corpus are inherited, and the stock runs through the full transaction or listing month, so it is not strictly prior information.

**Earlier sales history.** The sales profile panel extends to 1995 under the same fixed 2021–2024 Site Group projection: proximity is measured to the mapped overflow representatives as located in the study years, not to the assets, monitoring status or sewer network as they stood at the time of an earlier sale. No historical asset dating is attempted, so the earlier annual contrasts describe relative price paths of properties that are near today's mapped overflows. Address-based repeat matching over a 30-year history links more sales per property and is more exposed to redevelopment or re-addressing than the 2014-onward matching; the annual near/far support table shows where each year's contrast is drawn from.

**Identification and inference.** A publicity interpretation would require the absence of competing changes in the relative desirability of near locations; the property, month and MSOA × year effects and the annual profiles inform that assessment but do not establish it, and the joint pre-period test covers 2014–2018 relative to 2019 only, also on the expanded sales profile fit. Calendar-month effects do not remove national shocks with different near and far effects. LSOA clustering allows dependence within an LSOA, not arbitrary cross-LSOA dependence, and the residual-support measures diagnose how much and where focal variation remains without declaring adequate inference from sample size alone. Characteristic exclusions and controlled comparisons assess sensitivity; they do not show that conversions, matching error or selection have been removed. The short-window variant changes both the dates and the repeat membership and does not reproduce the existing cross-sectional baseline.

## Reproduce and locate outputs

```{r}
#| label: reproduce-values
#| include: false

fp <- results$metadata$fingerprint
runtime <- results$runtime
input_lines <- sprintf("`%s` (%s)", names(fp$inputs), fp$inputs)
```

The sales inputs are the 1995–2024 history and mapping. Regenerating them upstream follows a gated order, each step from the project root in the R 4.6.0 `rv` environment: `Rscript scripts/R/testing/verify_sales_profile_extension.R baseline` (once; refuses to overwrite a frozen baseline) and `sources` (validates the year-to-source manifest: both split parts for 1995–2013, the exact complete annual files for 2014–2024); `Rscript scripts/R/02_data_cleaning/clean_lr_house_price_data.R` (writes the paired candidates); `verify_sales_profile_extension.R overlap` (2014–2024 values and ids and the 2021–2024 study table must equal the baseline); a candidate mapping run, `Rscript -e 'source("scripts/R/06_analysis_datasets/repeat_sales.R"); main(repeat_sales_config(input_path = here::here("data", "processed", "house_price_long_run_candidate.parquet"), publish = FALSE))'`; `verify_sales_profile_extension.R mapping` (every baseline transaction keeps its repeat id); `verify_sales_profile_extension.R promote` (replaces the six sales artifacts as one unit; `rollback` restores the baseline). After the estimation render below, `verify_sales_profile_extension.R bundle` checks that the 40 scalar cells, their samples and settings and both rental profiles reproduce the baseline bundle at tolerance 1e-8.

The estimation path re-validates the inputs, re-estimates the grid, and writes the bundle and artifacts:

```bash
quarto render docs/reports/2026-09-19-001-long-run-public-attention-repeat-properties.qmd --to html
```

The presentation-only path loads the saved bundle and refuses it when any computational dependency changed, or when the bundle does not name an input the current configuration consumes; it re-exports the tables, figures and log when they do not carry the bundle's fingerprint:

```bash
quarto render docs/reports/2026-09-19-001-long-run-public-attention-repeat-properties.qmd --to html -P reestimate:false
```

The fixtures-only path runs the synthetic fixture checks alone (seconds, no data, no bundle) and stops after printing their table:

```bash
quarto render docs/reports/2026-09-19-001-long-run-public-attention-repeat-properties.qmd --to html -P fixtures_only:true
```

The bundle recorded `r format_seconds(results$metadata$runtime_seconds)` for the last estimation run (`r paste(sprintf("%s %s", results$markets$market, format_seconds(results$markets$runtime_seconds)), collapse = ", ")`); `r results$metadata$peak_memory_note`. Outputs, all gitignored under the `output/` symlink:

- `output/regs/long_run_public_attention/`: the results bundle (`r CONFIG$bundle_file`), written atomically and validated before it replaces the previous one.
- `output/tables/long_run_public_attention/`: CSVs for cells, profile coefficients, joint tests, residual support (and by year), the exclusion and variant ledgers, sample support, the readiness summary, the attention calendar and the input provenance; every row carries the run's combined fingerprint.
- `output/figures/long_run_public_attention/`: PDF figures (`coefficient_comparison.pdf`, `annual_profiles.pdf`, `attention_history_sales.pdf` when the calendar validated) at manuscript size with `run_fingerprint.txt` beside them. The sales panels of `annual_profiles.pdf` span 1995–2024 and the rental panels 2014–2023.
- The `annual_profiles_reference_2014.pdf` and `annual_profiles_reference_2021.pdf` views are regenerated from the validated bundle during each full report render, including cached renders, from the same expanded sales coefficients and covariance.
- `output/log/long_run_public_attention/run_log.txt`: runtime, fingerprint components, package versions and the fit log.

The combined fingerprint `` `r fp$combined` `` hashes four components: the content hashes of the consumed inputs (`r paste(input_lines, collapse = ", ")`); the code (`r paste(computational_chunk_labels(), collapse = ", ")` chunks and the sourced helpers `r paste(HELPER_FILES, collapse = ", ")`); the canonical analysis settings; and the computational package versions. Prose, display chunks, display packages and the `reestimate` switch are outside it.

The rest of this explanation cites the audit that preceded the plan (19 September 2026) and is not recomputed here. The same-day sales fix removed the 102,699 observations above in 50,327 address–date conflicts; on the same input it reduced groups with multiple observed property types from 90,073 to 77,319 (a 14.2% reduction). Other changes introduced content-stable string ids, rejected duplicate Land Registry transaction ids and removed 11,941 exact duplicate rental rows. On the full mappings the audit found property-type changes in 77,319 of 1,861,864 sales repeat properties (4.15%); for rentals, type changes in 81,056, bedroom changes in 109,500, bathroom changes in 74,416 and any change in 213,822 of 1,379,332 repeat properties (15.50%). Of the flagged sales groups, 66,376 included the `Other` category (85.85% of flags) and 11,483 had multiple specific residential codes, which suggests a classification component without proving the cause. A further 420,619 rental properties had missing-to-observed differences without an observed change. Across-date characteristic changes remain diagnostics, not automatic exclusions: `scripts/R/testing/test_repeat_transactions_contracts.R` preserves mixed-type groups, and the flags cannot distinguish real conversions, inconsistent classification and wrong address matches.
